object.definition: The learner acts in the same nonempty compact convex set $W\subset\mathbb R^d$ each round and is compared simultaneously with every comparator path $u_{1:T}\in W^T$. Losses are differentiable and exp-concave on $W$: $$\operatorname{diam}_2(W)\le D,\qquad e^{-\eta f_t(\cdot)}\ \text{on }W\text{ is concave},\qquad \|\nabla f_t(w)\|_2\le G\quad(\forall t,\ w\in W).$$ The upper bound holds for every admissible realized loss sequence; the recorded lower bound uses an oblivious sequence. For dimension optimality, $D,G,\eta$ are fixed independently of $d,T$.

operation.query_signature: Submit $w_t\in W$, incur $f_t(w_t)$, and then receive the full function $f_t$. Its values and gradients may subsequently be evaluated at other points, without observation noise. The public projection interface provides exact Mahalanobis projections for any positive definite metric $A\succ0$; each such projection has arithmetic cost $C_{\mathrm{proj}}(d)$. $$\Pi_W^A(z)\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{w\in W}(w-z)^{\mathsf T}A(w-z).$$ Inputs $d,T,D,G,\eta$, the set $W$, and its projection interface are public. Neither the comparator path $u_{1:T}$ nor its total path length $P_T^{(2)}$ is supplied. Past feedback may be stored and reused computationally; no unrevealed historical information or extra queries to exhausted samples are available beyond the explicitly declared within-round interface.

steps: Submit $w_t\in W$, incur $f_t(w_t)$, then receive the complete function $f_t$. The function and its gradient may subsequently be evaluated at other points; feedback is noiseless.
The public projection interface supports exact Mahalanobis projection in any positive-definite metric $A\succ0$. The arithmetic cost of one such projection is $C_{\mathrm{proj}}(d)$.
Public inputs are $d,T,D,G,\eta$, the set $W$, and its projection interface.
Neither the comparator path $u_{1:T}$ nor its total path length $P_T^{(2)}$ is supplied to the algorithm.

Received feedback may be stored and reused in computation. Unrevealed information cannot be requested from past rounds, and consumed random samples cannot receive additional queries. Current-round exceptions are limited to the explicitly supplied full-function access or same-sample two-point interface.
